overview: Two related but distinct helper molecules enzymes rely on — a broad structural/inorganic category and its organic subset.
genZNote: All coenzymes are cofactors. Not all cofactors get invited to the coenzyme club.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Any non-protein chemical compound (organic or inorganic) required for an enzyme's biological activity.
aspects.valueB: A specific type of organic cofactor, often derived from a vitamin, that assists catalysis, frequently by transferring a chemical group.

aspects.label: Chemical Nature
aspects.valueA: Can be an inorganic ion (e.g. Mg2+, Zn2+, Fe2+) or an organic molecule.
aspects.valueB: Always organic, often a vitamin derivative (e.g. NAD+ from niacin, FAD from riboflavin).

aspects.label: Binding to Enzyme
aspects.valueA: May be loosely or tightly bound, including as a prosthetic group.
aspects.valueB: Often binds loosely and transiently, acting as a substrate-like carrier that dissociates after the reaction.

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueA: Mg2+ for hexokinase, Zn2+ for carbonic anhydrase, heme (a prosthetic group) in catalase.

aspects.label: Relationship Between the Two
aspects.valueA: The broader umbrella term — includes metal ions and coenzymes alike.
aspects.valueB: A subset of cofactors, specifically the organic, vitamin-derived ones.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Broad category — includes metal ions and organic molecules.
aspects.valueB: Organic, usually vitamin-derived subset of cofactors.
